title: Rollout Rituals Chronicle (draft)
content:
Context and intent:

This doc collects a set of cross-functional "rituals" and small operational runbooks we want to standardize for LLM feature rollouts (canaries, micro‑exposures, A/B experiments) across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. It is intentionally informal — a living chronicle of things that work, things we tried, and unresolved tradeoffs.

Audience: product managers, release engineers, SRE, solutions engineering, instrumented owners (observability), and oncall.

Summary of the approach (one-liner):
- Treat rollout as choreography, not just traffic percentages: define rehearsal, exposure, observation windows, and a compact rollback script for each experiment.

Rituals (high level):
1) Preflight (owner: experiment author) — a reproducible checklist we expect before any traffic changes:
   - Validation: unit/runbook tests for routing, feature gates, and fallback behavior (jira: JIRA-ENG-1423).
   - Canary config baked in infra repo and reviewed (PR link above).
   - Observability smoke: dashboards exist and show baseline for 24h, SLO/alert thresholds chosen.
   - Stakeholders notified (PM, SRE, Legal if user-visible new behavior).

2) Rehearsal (owner: release engineer) — execute in a synthetic or staging slice with real traces where possible:
   - Synthetic generator replay for N minutes (match typical seq lengths).
   - Validate KV cache behavior and latency percentiles for long-tail sessions.
   - Run the canary script locally to verify rollback.

3) Micro-exposure (owner: product/exp owner) — small, timeboxed exposure; not purely static weight increases:
   - Start: 0.5% traffic for 30m or until 500 sessions, whichever first.
   - Observe: telemetry ramp and user-visible correctness metrics.
   - Scale pattern: geometric increase (0.5%, 2%, 8%, 25%) with at least one observation window between moves.

4) A/B windows for product signal validation (owner: data/analysis):
   - Run at stable weight for a minimum of 24–72 hours to capture diurnal and geo variance.
   - Use pre-registered primary metric (e.g., rerank CTR delta, safety violations per 1k responses, latency P99) and guard metrics (cost per request, error-rate).

Operational checklists (copyable):
- Before ramp: verify alerts: p50/p90/p99 latency, 5xx count, token cost drift, hallucination indicator (eval harness mismatch > X%).
- During ramp: watch three golden signals plus model quality: throughput, latency, error-rate; and one business metric that matters to the feature.
- Escalation cadence: first 30m — pair to oncall Slack channel; 30–120m — page SRE if threshold exceeded; >120m — convene rapid sync with PM/engineering/ops.

Stoplight thresholds (suggested starting points):
- GREEN: p99 latency change < 15% relative to baseline; 5xx rate < 0.05% absolute; model-quality drift (eval harness) < 1pp.
- YELLOW: p99 latency change 15–35% OR 5xx rate 0.05–0.2% OR quality drift 1–5pp — pause ramp, collect logs, triage.
- RED: p99 latency change > 35% OR 5xx rate > 0.2% OR quality drift > 5pp — rollback immediately to last known-good variant.

Rollback script (short & prescriptive):
- Who: release engineer oncall or product owner authorized.
- What: revert traffic split to previous config (exactly as codified in the last commit), kill canary pods if present, and switch to fallback model variant if configured.
- Communications: post to #release-ops with brief cause, metrics snapshot, and link to incident doc.
- Postmortem: owner to file a 1–page postmortem within 72 hours.

Traffic choreography primitives (examples):
- Weighted static split (A/B): 50/50 for cosmetic experiments; ensure randomization key stable across requests.
- Session sticky slice: for chat-like experiences, stick session_id to variant for entire session to avoid cross-variant noise.
- Timebox slice: open/close exposure windows tied to UTC calendar to align with infra maintenance windows.

Example micro-exposure plan (copy/paste):
- Name: rerank-v2-microexp-2026-02
- Variants: control=r1, treatment=r2
- Start: 0.5% global traffic at 2026-02-18T15:00Z for 30m
- Metrics: primary=topic_ctr, guard=latency_p99, cost=token_per_response
- Ramp rule: 0.5% -> 2% after 30m stable -> 8% after next 60m stable -> 25% only after 24h stable
- Rollback criteria: if any RED threshold triggered or >10% relative drop in topic_ctr after 24h

Signal instrumentation suggestions (observability team):
- Tag telemetry with variant, model_version, region, and routing_policy.
- Emit a compact bundle per request: {variant, latency_ms, tokens_out, error_code, eval_signal} where eval_signal is a small integer enumerating heuristics (toxicity, hallucination heuristics, rerank-mismatch).
- Include sampler of full traces (1 in 1000) for offline QA.

Comms snippets (to use in Slack/email):
- Prelaunch note: "Starting micro-exposure 'rerank-v2' at 0.5% on 2026-02-18T15:00Z. Observability dashboard: <link>. Please stand by in #release-ops for 45m."
- Pause/Throttle: "Pausing rerank-v2 ramp: observed p99 latency increase crossing yellow threshold. Triage in #release-ops"
- Rollback: "Rollback executed for rerank-v2 at 2026-02-18T16:22Z due to quality drift >5pp. See incident doc: <link>."

Roles & responsibilities (short):
- Experiment owner: author of hypothesis, primary contact for metric interpretation.
- Release engineer: executes ramping and rollback, owns runbook scripts.
- Observability lead: sets dashboards & alerts, verifies instrumentation.
- Oncall SRE: infrastructure-level mitigations (scaling, capacity fallbacks).
- Data/analysis: producing interim analysis and confidence intervals (p-values not required for quick safety decisions).

Open questions / tradeoffs (explicit):
- How long should micro-exposures be for low-traffic regions? (500 sessions might be too long to reach in small geos)
- What minimum statistical standard for product metrics should gate a multi-day exposure? (practical vs. theoretical tradeoffs)
- Should cost-per-request be part of early gates or only post-rollout optimization?

Immediate action items / next steps: (TODOs)
- [ ] Instrument eval_signal enums and publish dictionary (owner: observability)
- [ ] Add a 'safe-fallback' model variant to the infra repo for every new model deployment (owner: serving-runtime)
- [ ] Bake micro-exposure templates into the console rollout UI (owner: product-console)
- [ ] Draft a short-runbook snippet for customer success to use when customers see behavior variance (owner: customer-success)

Historical notes / experiments we've tried (short journal):
- 2025-11: tried aggressive 10%->50% ramp; caused cache-pressure latency spike in dedicated pools — learned to include KV cache pressure metric.
- 2025-08: session-sticky rollout reduced metric noise for chat product; added session_id hashing primitive.

Closing thought: treat this doc as a choreography script library. The more short, prescriptive scripts we have (and the fewer implicit handoffs), the faster and safer our rollouts will be.

Links referenced (quick):
- Experiment Registry: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/display/RO/Experiment-Registry
- Rollout scripts PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts/pull/87
- Incident template: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/display/OPS/Incident-Template

Notes to self: add a tiny glossary entry mapping our "ritual" terms (rehearsal, micro-exposure, choreography) to the console UI fields.
